argument: No deterministic protocol can guarantee consensus termination in a fully asynchronous message-passing system if even one process may crash, despite reliable channels. An adversarial schedule can keep the system bivalent indefinitely.
boundary: The result does not preclude safety, randomization, partial synchrony, or failure detectors.
It is a worst-case termination result, not a claim that consensus never works.
claim: No deterministic protocol can guarantee consensus termination in a fully asynchronous message-passing system if even one process may crash, despite reliable channels. An adversarial schedule can keep the system bivalent indefinitely.
interpretation: A consensus claim should state synchrony, fault, and liveness assumptions. Benign benchmark schedules do not prove worst-case termination.
